title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Maryville traditions, including current campus events and clearly labeled historical practices.

cards.title: Maryville Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide Saints celebration
cards.notes: Watch Maryville’s Homecoming page for the next schedule, then choose a public activity that fits your visit and participation preferences.
cards.short_summary: A current signature Maryville tradition that brings campus and alumni communities together.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville identifies Homecoming as one of its signature traditions.
cards.access_notes: Event timing and individual activity access vary; consult Maryville’s Homecoming page.

cards.title: Cram Jam
cards.subtitle: Finals-week breakfast and study gathering
cards.notes: During finals, look for the campus announcement and join classmates for the study-focused breakfast gathering when it is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: Maryville’s finals-week gathering pairs studying with breakfast and prizes.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville calls Cram Jam one of its most cherished traditions and describes it as a Finals Week gathering in Gander Dining Hall.
cards.source_title: Cram Jam is Back! — Maryville MPress
cards.access_notes: The cited report anticipated Spring Cram Jam; confirm the current semester’s event details with Student Experience.

cards.title: Ring the Saints Success Bell
cards.subtitle: Student Success, University Library
cards.notes: If you have a milestone to celebrate, contact your Life Coach or visit Student Success to arrange a bell ringing and mark the moment.
cards.short_summary: A bell-ringing ritual for students’ academic and personal milestones.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville introduced the Saints Success Bell as a tradition for students to celebrate accomplishments through Student Success.
cards.source_title: Let’s Celebrate Saints Success — Maryville MPress
cards.access_notes: The source directs students to email a Life Coach to schedule or stop by Student Success in the University Library.

cards.title: The Annual Foam Party
cards.subtitle: Historical campus event tradition
cards.notes: Treat this as a historical Maryville event; check the current campus-events calendar before planning around it or assuming it will recur.
cards.short_summary: A campus foam-dance event that Maryville described as an annual tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville reported that its annual Foam Party was considered a Maryville tradition.
cards.source_title: Maryville Students Get Organized – and Set Record — Maryville MPress
cards.access_notes: Historical documentation only; current recurrence, location, and participation details were not verified.

cards.title: 1000 Saints Night
cards.subtitle: Historic basketball fundraising night
cards.notes: Use the university events calendar to see whether a related athletics fundraiser is scheduled; do not assume this historical format is current.
cards.short_summary: A Maryville basketball-night fundraiser documented in the university’s 2017 report.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s 2017 President’s Report describes the fourth annual 1000 Saints Night, a basketball-game fundraiser for Kids Rock Cancer.
cards.access_notes: Historical documentation only; current recurrence and admission arrangements were not verified.

cards.title: May Crowning at the Grotto
cards.subtitle: Discontinued Maryville Academy tradition
cards.notes: Explore the University Archives story and photographs to understand this former campus ritual; it is not a current student activity.
cards.short_summary: A yearly ceremony at the former campus in which a student crowned the grotto’s Mary statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville Archives identifies May Crowning as a yearly tradition and states that it ended in 1962.
cards.source_title: Scrapbook Depicts Early Life at Maryville Academy — Maryville MPress
cards.access_notes: Discontinued in 1962 after occurring once at the west St. Louis County campus.

cards.title: Play Cache-cache
cards.subtitle: Historic French-style school game
cards.notes: Read the university history for this former student pastime and its French educational context; it is presented as archival history, not programming.
cards.short_summary: Maryville’s early students played a French-style game the university describes as a glorified hide-and-seek.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s history says French customs included after-school cache-cache, described as a glorified hide-and-seek game.
cards.access_notes: Historic practice from Maryville’s early French-influenced school; no current activity was verified.

cards.title: The Goûter Snack
cards.subtitle: Historic French school custom
cards.notes: Use the university history to trace this former snack-time custom and its place in Maryville’s early French-influenced school life.
cards.short_summary: A French snack custom documented among Maryville’s early school practices.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s history lists daily snacks, called goûter, among the French customs that prevailed at the school.
cards.access_notes: Historic practice only; no current dining program or offering was verified.

cards.title: French at the Table
cards.subtitle: Historic Maryville dining-room custom
cards.notes: Read the university history alongside the school’s French lycee model to place this former dining-room practice in its original context.
cards.short_summary: Early Maryville students were encouraged to use French during meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s history states that French was taught at all levels and girls were encouraged to speak it, especially during meals.
cards.access_notes: Historic practice from the early school; no current requirement or event was verified.

cards.title: Celebrate the Congés
cards.subtitle: Historic French holiday observances
cards.notes: Consult Maryville’s institutional history for this former French holiday custom rather than treating it as a current campus-calendar event.
cards.short_summary: Traditional French holidays were part of Maryville’s early French-influenced school culture.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryville’s history says traditional French holidays, called congés, were among the customs that prevailed throughout the school.
cards.access_notes: Historic practice only; current observance dates or programming were not verified.
